name: Kit Clark Furniture
old_description: It is the honor of my career to bring beauty and balance into my client's homes. The true reward in doing what I do is seeing the impact my furniture has on the people who interact with it on a daily basis.
about:
Kit Clark Furniture operates from a studio in North Yarmouth, Maine, a rural community northwest of Portland. The business traces its roots to the early 2000s when founder Kit Clark opened a shop in Bozeman, Montana, after studying furniture design at the Penland School of Crafts in North Carolina. Clark relocated the operation to North Ferrisburgh, Vermont, in 2000, then moved again in the spring of 2016 to the current Maine location. A lifelong woodworker, Clark earned an associate degree in forestry from the University of New Hampshire and a bachelor’s in mine land reclamation from Montana State University, later apprenticing under his uncle, master carpenter Robert Clark, and studying Sam Maloof–style rocking chairs with chairwright Hal Taylor in 2007.

The studio produces bespoke, handcrafted furniture ranging from sculpted rocking chairs and dining sets to tables, beds, bedroom suites, bookcases, and custom accessories. Each piece is built to order using traditional joinery and a selection of domestic and exotic woods chosen by the client. Clark works alone or with minimal assistance, fabricating every component in-house and finishing each item to a museum-quality standard. Output is measured in individual commissions rather than volume runs, with no published capacity figures.

The clientele consists primarily of residential customers across the continental United States and Canada, including homeowners and interior designers seeking one-of-a-kind heirloom pieces. Testimonials reference clients in North Carolina, Singapore, and Massachusetts, and the company offers in-home design consultations for local projects. Shipping is arranged worldwide wherever freight can reach.

Clark cites a lifetime guarantee—valid for as long as the original purchaser or their family owns the piece—as a core differentiator, along with the ability to recreate any gallery design in alternative wood combinations. The founder’s design philosophy draws on the fluid forms of nature, aiming to bring the peace of the outdoors into the home.

name: Klingspor's Woodworking Shop
old_description: Updated weekly! Don't miss another sale - sign up for our email now.
about:
Klingspor's Woodworking Shop operates a retail location in Hickory, North Carolina, at 856 21st Street Drive SE. The business was founded in 1999 and serves as a specialty store for woodworking tools, supplies, and education. Ownership details and founder names are not publicly disclosed.

The shop stocks a wide range of woodworking products including abrasives (sandpaper, sanding discs, belts, and pads), router and saw bits, blades, carving and turning tools, cabinet-making supplies, finishing products, hardware, power tools, dust collection equipment, sharpening stones, safety gear, and both common and exotic woods. In addition to retail sales, the Hickory store hosts in-store woodworking classes led by staff and guest instructors, catering to all skill levels. The facility also provides meeting space for several regional woodworking clubs.

The customer base spans hobbyists, professional woodworkers, woodturners, carvers, and pyrography artists. Clubs that meet at the store include the Southeastern Pyrography Association, the North Carolina Woodturners Association (a chapter of the American Association of Woodturners), the Catawba Valley Woodcarvers, and the Western Piedmont Woodcrafters. These groups draw members from across North Carolina and neighboring states.

The company emphasizes weekly updated specials and a community-focused approach, combining product sales with hands-on learning and club gatherings. No specific founding mission or differentiator beyond this retail-and-education model is stated.

name: Knectiv
old_description: Hardware manufacturing, managed from engineering to production.
about:
Knectiv operates from Austin, Texas. The company was founded by Nicholas J. Frank, who serves as CEO, and Michael Lally, co‑founder. Together they built a firm that connects product engineering with global manufacturing execution, aiming to simplify hardware commercialization for clients.

The company provides end‑to‑end hardware manufacturing management, spanning product engineering, design for manufacturability, PCB fabrication and assembly, plastic injection molding, component sourcing, and turnkey production. Knectiv coordinates manufacturing globally, offering U.S.‑side accountability with production execution in China when needed, and supports programs from prototype through scale‑up.

Knectiv serves industrial, medical, consumer, automotive, audio, and connected‑hardware markets. Its customers include Swiss medical‑device maker GETS, audio‑technology firm Merging Technologies, air‑quality instrumentation company Zefon International, and automotive supplier CEBI Micromotors. The portfolio features devices such as the HemataStat microhematocrit centrifuge, MOHE LFIA reader, CO2EFFICIENT endoscopic insufflator, and Bluetooth‑enabled Elmore pedal.

Knectiv differentiates itself through a unified approach that consolidates engineering, supply chain, quality, and logistics under a single point of contact. The firm states that this model delivers simplified management, consistent quality, and greater efficiency, allowing clients to focus on innovation while Knectiv handles manufacturing complexity.

Knock On Wood Furniture is a family-owned and operated business based in Smithfield, Rhode Island. Founded in 1988, the company has served the Blackstone Valley area for over three decades.

The company specializes in finished and unfinished solid wood furniture, offering pieces such as desks, entertainment centers, bedroom sets, dining room sets, kitchen chairs, tables, cabinets, and pantries. It provides custom finishing services, including a wide range of stain and paint colors with color-matching capabilities. The business operates a showroom where customers can browse products.

Knock On Wood Furniture primarily serves residential customers in the Blackstone Valley region, supplying furniture for kitchens, bedrooms, and dining rooms. Its customer base includes homeowners and possibly local retailers, though the company emphasizes direct showroom sales.

The company highlights its long-standing local presence and custom finishing flexibility as key differentiators, though it does not explicitly state a founding mission beyond serving the community.

old_description: Farmers, landscapers, property maintenance, construction contractors, and homeowners have counted on Knoxland Equipment since 1962 to be their one stop shop. about:
Knoxland Equipment has operated from Warner, New Hampshire since 1962. The dealership was established to serve the region's agricultural and property-maintenance customers and has remained a locally owned business for over six decades. No founder names or ownership structure are disclosed in public records.

The company stocks and sells tractors from Mahindra and LS, zero-turn and walk-behind mowers from Ferris and Bad Boy, and a range of power equipment and attachments from brands including Briggs & Stratton, Land Pride, Hiniker, Milwaukee, and RedMax. A full-service department provides repair and maintenance for all makes and models, handling everything from routine service to major overhauls. The shop also supplies replacement parts and accessories for the brands it carries.

Customers span farming, landscaping, property-maintenance, construction, and residential sectors. The dealership serves commercial contractors, municipal crews, and individual property owners throughout central New Hampshire, offering both equipment sales and ongoing service support.

Knoxland positions itself as a one-stop shop for equipment sales, parts, and service, emphasizing its ability to service any brand regardless of where it was purchased. The company highlights its long-standing presence in the community as a factor in customer retention.

name: Kulicke & Soffa Industries Inc.
old_description: Kulicke and Soffa is a global leader in semiconductor assembly technology, advancing device performance across automotive, compute, industrial, memory and communications markets. Founded on innovation in 1951, K&S is uniquely positioned to overcome increasingly dynamic process challenges - creating and delivering long-term value by aligning technology with opportunity.
about:
Kulicke & Soffa Industries Inc. was founded in 1951 in Fort Washington, Pennsylvania. The company began as an innovator in semiconductor assembly technology and has since grown into a global supplier of equipment and solutions for the semiconductor packaging industry.

The company designs and manufactures semiconductor assembly equipment, including wire bonding, die bonding, thermocompression bonding, and ultrasonic assembly systems. Its product portfolio also encompasses advanced dispensing solutions, aftermarket products, repair and refurbishment services, and spare parts supply. K&S operates globally, serving customers across multiple continents with a focus on advanced packaging technologies such as fluxless thermocompression bonding and co-packaged optics assembly.

K&S serves customers in the automotive, compute, industrial, memory, and communications markets. Its equipment is used by semiconductor manufacturers and assembly houses producing devices for applications ranging from automotive electronics to high-performance computing and artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Founded on a commitment to innovation, the company emphasizes aligning technology with opportunity to overcome dynamic process challenges. Recent recognitions include a SEMI Award for North America for breakthrough fluxless thermocompression bonding technology, underscoring its focus on pioneering capabilities that redefine semiconductor assembly and packaging.

name: Kulite Semiconductor Products
old_description: Visit the Reference Library for Handbooks, Manuals, Installation Instructions, Technical Papers and More
about:
Kulite Semiconductor Products, Inc. was founded in 1959 by Dr. Anthony D. Kurtz in Leonia, New Jersey, just outside New York City. A physicist with degrees from MIT, Dr. Kurtz left Honeywell to establish a high‑technology company focused on pressure transduction. The business remains family‑founded and woman‑owned, now led by his widow, Nora Kurtz.

The company designs and manufactures pressure transducers, sensors, and switches for extreme environments. Its product line spans pressure ranges from 1 to 60,000 PSI, operating temperatures from ‑320 °F to 932 °F, and configurations including submersible, redundant, and hermetically sealed units. Kulite holds over 400 patents and operates a 200,000‑square‑foot, three‑building campus that houses research, manufacturing, and corporate offices, employing over 800 people.

Kulite serves aerospace and defense (commercial airliners such as the Boeing 747, military aircraft), automotive test and motorsport (Formula One, IndyCar), space exploration, marine, oil exploration, coal mining, and process‑control industries. Customers include OEMs, racing teams, and government agencies requiring high‑reliability pressure measurement.

The firm emphasizes that its differentiation lies in solving difficult pressure‑measurement problems: "whenever pressure or force needs to be measured, Kulite comes up with a solution." It claims to be the world’s largest supplier of aerospace transducers and points to its ongoing R&D investment, university partnerships, and thousands of custom designs delivered since 1959.

name: Kyana Packaging Solutions
old_description: Kyana Packaging Solutions was founded in 1976 as Kyana Industrial Supply by Dave and Inez White in their home. Dave White believed that he could bring greater value to his customers than was available in the market, so he left his job to start Kyana Industrial Supply (known today as Kyana Packaging Solutions).
about:
Kyana Packaging Solutions traces its roots to 1976, when Dave and Inez White founded Kyana Industrial Supply in their Louisville, Kentucky home. Dave White left his previous job convinced he could deliver greater value to customers than the market offered, and the business grew from that residential start into a multi-division packaging supplier.

Today the company operates three interconnected divisions. Kyana Packaging Solutions stocks and sells a broad range of packaging materials — corrugated boxes, tapes, poly bags, stretch film, cushioning, shrink wrap, cold-chain packaging, labels, strapping, safety and janitorial supplies — and also supplies packaging equipment. Bethlehem Die Cutting produces custom die‑cut components, while ASR Solutions provides third‑party logistics, kitting and assembly services that turn parts into ready‑to‑ship products. The combined footprint includes warehousing, conversion equipment and fulfillment capabilities, though specific facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

The customer base spans manufacturers, e‑commerce shippers, food and pharmaceutical companies needing cold‑chain solutions, and any operation that requires custom corrugated or die‑cut parts, kitting, or outsourced fulfillment. The company’s packaging assessment service helps clients optimize their packaging spend and performance.

The founding principle — delivering greater value than available elsewhere — remains the stated differentiator. The White family’s original vision was to offer hands‑on support and a wider product range than competitors, a philosophy that now extends across the Kyana ecosystem of supplies, conversion and logistics.

old_description: 京セラの電子部品事業の一翼を担うKYOCERA AVX Components Corporation（本社：米国）は、電子デバイス関連製品の強固な技術基盤と豊富なラインアップを有し、開発から製造、販売までをグローバルに展開しています。
about:
Kyocera Electronic Devices LLC operates from Fountain Inn, South Carolina, as the U.S. headquarters of KYOCERA AVX Components Corporation, the American subsidiary of Japan's Kyocera Corporation responsible for its electronic components business. The entity serves as the North American base for Kyocera's global electronic device operations.

The company designs, manufactures, and sells a broad range of electronic components, including connectors, timing devices such as crystal oscillators and SAW filters, capacitors (multilayer ceramic, polymer, and tantalum), inductors, circuit protection devices, RF/microwave components, and sensors and controls. Its product portfolio spans thousands of part numbers developed for applications from consumer electronics to aerospace, with manufacturing and sales coordinated globally.

Customers come from automotive (including Bluetooth Low Energy wireless battery management systems, advanced driver-assistance, and infotainment), smartphones, tablets, wearable devices, communication modules, general industrial equipment, data-center and AI servers, robotics, and aerospace/space programs. The company highlights its automotive-grade components qualified to AEC-Q200 alongside commercial-grade offerings.

Kyocera emphasizes a strong technical foundation built on materials science and high-frequency design, enabling miniaturized, low-power solutions such as differential clock oscillators operating at 0.9 V and multi-band SAW triplexers that save board space in advanced positioning and communication equipment. The firm also maintains RoHS and REACH compliance and holds ISO/IATF certifications across its facilities.

name: L Sweet Lumber Company Inc.
old_description: In 1885, civil engineer Leprilete Sweet founded L. Sweet & Company, in the Olneyville section of Providence, RI.
about:
L. Sweet Lumber Company Inc. traces its roots to 1885 when civil engineer Leprilete Sweet founded L. Sweet & Company in the Olneyville section of Providence, Rhode Island. Sweet purchased a wooden frame building from the Church of the Messiah, moved it to Harris Avenue for railroad access, and established a storefront that remains in use today. The business, now in its fifth generation, continues as a local, family-owned operation.

The company stocks framing and finish lumber sourced from domestic and international forests, and maintains an extensive inventory of moulding profiles, including historical patterns specific to the Providence area. It also supplies doors, windows, skylights, hardwood flooring, decking (as a TimberTech/Azek dealer), cedar shingles, clapboard siding, and a range of building materials. Services include on-time delivery via a fleet of trucks, trade credit, estimates, site visits, contractor referrals, blade sharpening, key cutting, lock keying, and a showroom with displays and samples.

L. Sweet Lumber serves the building and construction industry across Southern New England, catering to contractors, builders, and homeowners. Its customer base includes professionals seeking historical moulding profiles for restoration projects and dealers of specialty decking and siding products.

The company emphasizes its long-standing commitment to service, selection, quality, and competitive pricing, noting that customer loyalty has persisted since its founding. It positions itself as a one-stop shop for lumber and building materials, backed by knowledgeable staff and personalized service.
